summary: Edward Clive Bayley worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College and the East India Company College (~1840–1842). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1842) and was Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta (1869–1874).

Edward Conze was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. at Cologne under Max Scheler, also studying under Jaspers, Cassirer, and Walleser. He held posts at London, Wisconsin-Madison, and Washington, and was Vice-President of the Buddhist Society.

Edward Delavan Perry was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University and under Rudolf von Roth at the University of Tübingen. He served as Dean of the Faculty of Philosophy at Columbia University from 1880 to 1931.

Edward Denison Ross was a linguist, Tibetologist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at UCL and under Schefer, Renan, and Nöldeke in Strasbourg. He held posts at UCL, Aliah University, the National Archives of India, and SOAS.

Edward Douglas Maclagan was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at Winchester College and New College (~1882–1886). He served as Chancellor of the University of the Punjab (1919–1924) and President of the Royal Asiatic Society (1925–1928).

Edward Edwards specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Bala Theological College, at Aberystwyth University under Hermann Ethé, and at Christ's College, Cambridge. He worked as an Assistant at the British Museum from 1904 to 1935.

Edward Elbridge Salisbury specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Yale and in Europe under Burnouf, Bopp, Silvestre de Sacy, Lassen, and Woolsey. He was Professor of Arabic and Sanskrit at Yale (1841–1854) and President of the American Oriental Society (1873–1880).

Edward Evan Evans-Pritchard worked in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Exeter College, Oxford, and at the London School of Economics under Bronisław Malinowski. He held academic posts at LSE, Cairo University, Cambridge, and Oxford (1946–1970).

Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate under Roderick S. Bucknell. He has held academic posts at the University of Queensland and the University of Sydney.

Edward Garrett is a scholar of linguistics and Tibetology who completed his Ph.D. at UCLA under Carson T. Schütze and Dominique Sportiche, later mentored by Anna Szabolcsi. He held research assistant posts at UCLA (1996–2000) and the University of Virginia (2000–2001).

Edward Geoffrey Parrinder was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Richmond College (1929–1932). He served as Senior Lecturer at the University of Ibadan (~1948–1958) and became a Reader at King's College London in 1958.

Edward Granville Browne was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. Educated at Cambridge, where he studied under E. B. Cowell, E. H. Palmer, and William Wright, he served as Lecturer in Persian and Sir Thomas Adams's Professor of Arabic.

Edward Green Balfour worked in Indology and other fields. He was educated at Montrose Academy and the University of Edinburgh (~1831–1834). He founded the Government Museum, Chennai, serving as its Superintendent from 1850, and was a Fellow of the University of Madras.

Edward H. Schafer was a Sinologist who studied at UCLA, UC Berkeley, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Harvard. He taught in the Department of Oriental Languages at UC Berkeley (~1947–1984) and served as president of the American Oriental Society (1975–1976).

Edward H. Spieker was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. Educated at Baltimore City College, he completed his A.B. and Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins University, where he served as Associate Professor of Greek and Latin from 1880 to 1918.

Edward Hamilton Johnston was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at New College, Oxford, under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. After serving in the Indian Civil Service (~1909–1922), he became Boden Professor of Sanskrit and a Fellow of Balliol College in 1937.

Edward Henry Palmer worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Sayyid Abdallah and at St John's College, Cambridge, later serving as Cambridge's Lord Almoner’s Professor of Arabic from 1871 to 1881.
Edward Hincks was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He received his education at Midleton College and Trinity College Dublin, where he completed his B.A. between 1807 and 1812.

Edward James Rapson was an Indologist, historian, and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at St John's College, Cambridge, under Cecil Bendall and Edward Byles Cowell. He held posts at the British Museum, UCL, and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Cambridge (1906–1936).

Edward John Thompson was a scholar of Indology and history who studied at Richmond College. He taught English and served as Vice-Principal at Bankura Christian College, lectured in Bengali at Oxford (from 1923), and was a Research Fellow at Oriel College (1936–1940).
